items.title: Type of transport buses when building a route

labels.name: Public Transport
labels.description: Bus, trolleybus, train, tram, metro, subway, light rail

items.body:
- [x] I have searched for similar, already existing issues.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When planning a route in Organic Maps, the available transport modes include only metro (and walking/cycling/driving modes). However, **buses** are one of the most common and accessible forms of public transport in many cities. The lack of bus routing makes the app impractical for urban trips without a private car.

I often need to plan a bus route, but I have to switch to other apps (Google Maps, Yandex Maps, etc.), which is inconvenient.

**Describe the ideal solution**

Add a **"Bus"** option to the transport selection section when planning a route. Ideally, the route should take bus stops, schedules (if available in OSM), and travel time into account.

It would also be nice to have **combined options** (bus + metro, bus + walking, etc.), but the bare minimum is a separate bus mode.

**Describe alternatives you have considered**

Currently I use:
- OSMAnd (has buses, but the UI is more complex);
- third‑party apps (Google Maps, 2GIS, Yandex Maps);
- I plan a walking route and mentally adjust it by bus stops — very inconvenient.

**Additional context**

This is not a bug but a feature request. I understand that public transport routing is more complex than car navigation, but even basic bus support (using the OSM graph) would significantly improve the Organic Maps experience in cities. Thank you!

items.title: Lazy routing option: allow me to specify the exact route and only optimize between waypoints

labels.name: Routing
labels.description: Route building issues, e.g. valid route, valid ETA

items.body:
When trying to create a specific walking route (for a walking club, one that is _known beforehand)_ Organic Maps is eagerly trying to complete the route from the points I entered. As a result, OM creates a route that makes no sense.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Set the pedestrian mode
2. Set the start point somewhere on a path in a park or on a street
3. Continue by adding intermediate waypoints
4. OM at first follows the shortest path to the next point, but eventually tries some random path that reconnects to the original path and messes up completely.

**Expected behaviour**
What I want is for OM to only create a short straight section along the walking path, between the previous waypoint and the last waypoint I entered. Once I enter the end, it should connect the last waypoint to the end, completing a path along a predetermined set of waypoints. The path can be A to B or circular.

**System information:**
 - Operating system: Linux Mint 22.3 - Xfce 64-bit
 - Organic Maps version: 2026.05.28-1-d81f9197-dirty-Linux
 - Device Model: Acer Aspire desktop

**Additional context**
It seems the routing algorithm works very well to create an optimal route from A to B with perhaps an intermediate point or two for guidance. My use case however is to create a route that is _already specified_ (by the walking club, it is a "sanctioned" route that has to be just so.) The algorithm seems to get confused by multiple intermediate points.

Perhaps a good solution would be to have a "lazy routing" option. Use the existing algorithm but only between pairs of intermediate waypoints. Then it would connect them without trying to optimize the whole route.

items.title: Walking mode route should ignore vehicle-only gates

labels.name: Routing
labels.description: Route building issues, e.g. valid route, valid ETA

items.body: **Describe the issue** On a hiking route that shares a segment with a road with restricted vehicle access, OM should respect the Allow Access tags from OSM that indicate roads/gates are open to pedestrians and/or cyclists (depending on routing mode). **Steps to reproduce** Route from end of NF Development Road 5510 where it meets Hansen Ridge Trail (47.359536, -121.539149) Route to Hansen Creek Trailhead (47.363961, -121.531193) Set mode to Walking **Expected behaviour** The router should use the shorter road segment. Adding an intermediate point on the road may force OM to use the segment, but this extra step shouldn't be necessary. **Screenshots** **System information:** - Operating system and its version: Android 17 - Organic Maps version: 2026.08.27-18-Google - Device Model: Google Pixel 7 **Additional context** The above example is part of an official hiking loop passes through a locked gate, and follows a short segment of road. Both the road and gate are marked as foot:yes, bicycles:yes in the Allow Access tags. Yet OM tries hard to avoid the road and route the long way around. After discussion via the Telegram group, we think it's the locked:yes tag on the gate itself that confuses the router. When the tags explicitly include foot:yes and bicycles:yes, the locked:yes tag should apply only to automobiles, and allow passage for pedestrians and cyclists. When the tags include foot:yes (but not bicycles:yes), the locked:yes tag should allow passage by pedestrians, but block automobiles and cyclists. When the tags include bicycles:yes (but not foot:yes), the locked:yes tag should allow passage by cyclists, but block automobiles and pedestrians. Barrier: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2428416980#map=20/47.3642863/-121.5318366&layers=VD with tags: ``` barrier=gate bicycle=yes foot=yes locked=yes material=metal ```

items.title: [ios] Support Core Spotlight category synonyms without duplicate results
items.body:
Core Spotlight category indexing is intentionally limited to the primary category name for each preferred device language because synonym indexing produces unreliable system search results on recent iOS versions.

Observed on a physical iPhone:
- `alternateNames` and `keywords` do not make synonyms discoverable in the system Spotlight UI.
- A separate `Поесть` item and the primary `Где поесть` item are both returned for the `Поесть` query, even though they open the same category.
- Shared synonym items with identical titles, such as `Food` or `Еда`, may disappear from the results entirely.
- Short terms such as `eat` and `Еда` are not returned.

Investigate a reliable, maintainable way to index useful synonyms without duplicate results or ambiguous mappings between categories. The solution should support all preferred device languages, preserve stable category deep links, and be validated on a physical device with primary, unique, contained, shared, and short synonyms.

items.title: Cannot plan closed-loop routes (duplicate point); route rebuild loops after brief GPS outage
items.body:
I ran into two separate navigation/routing bugs and traced both to their root cause
in the source. I'm attaching a draft patch — I have **not** compiled or tested it
(no local build environment), so please review, adjust, and test before considering
a merge. Happy to answer questions or iterate based on feedback.

## Bug 1: Cannot plan a closed-loop route (same point can't be re-added)

**Symptom:** Planning a route that returns to its starting point (A → B → C → A) is
impossible: tapping the start point again while adding a stop doesn't add it, it only
offers to remove the existing route point. Workaround found online: save/export the
route, then re-import it — but a re-imported route can't be started/navigated directly.

**Root cause:** `android/app/src/main/java/.../PlacePageController.java`,
`updateButtons()`. Whenever the tapped `MapObject` resolves to an existing route point
(`RoutingController.isRoutePoint()`), the method unconditionally shows only
`ROUTE_REMOVE`, regardless of whether the app is currently in an active
"pick a location for a new/replacement stop" state (`isWaitingPoiPick()`, entered via
the "Add stop" button). So re-tapping any existing route point — including the start,
to close a loop — always offers only removal.

The underlying routing engine (`RoutingManager::AddRoutePoint` in
`libs/map/routing_manager.cpp`) has no restriction on duplicate coordinates; this is
purely a UI-layer limitation.

**Proposed fix:** only fall into the `ROUTE_REMOVE`-only branch when the app is *not*
in `isWaitingPoiPick()` state, so the normal add/replace branch handles it instead.

## Bug 2: Route recalculation loops after a brief GPS outage

**Symptom:** During pedestrian navigation with intermediate stops, a brief GPS signal
loss can cause the app to loop on "recalculating route", repeatedly trying to route
the user *back* to a stop already passed. Manually deleting the already-passed route
points was the only way to recover.

**Root cause:** `libs/routing/routing_session.cpp` / `libs/routing/checkpoints.cpp`.
An intermediate checkpoint is only marked "passed" inside
`RoutingSession::PassCheckpoints()`, which only runs when `Route::MoveIterator()`
successfully matches the GPS fix to the route polyline
(`RoutingSession::OnLocationPositionChanged`). The pedestrian matching threshold is
only 20 m (`routing_settings.cpp`), so a fix reacquired after an outage can easily fall
outside range for a few updates — if the user walked past a checkpoint during that
window, it never gets marked passed.

Once `m_moveAwayCounter > kOnRouteMissedCount` triggers a forced rebuild
(`RoutingManager::CheckLocationForRouting`), the rebuild still uses the stale
checkpoint list (`IndexRouter::DoCalculateRoute` iterates from
`checkpoints.GetPassedIdx()`), so the already-visited checkpoint is still mandatory in
the new route — sending the user backwards, and repeating on every subsequent reroute
if position keeps drifting.

**Proposed fix:** a new `RoutingSession::AdvancePassedCheckpointsIfNeeded()`, called
right before a forced rebuild. Heuristic: walk forward through remaining checkpoints
and mark one "passed" if current position is unambiguously closer (beyond the matching
threshold, to avoid flip-flopping) to the *following* checkpoint than to it — only
possible if the user already passed it. The loop stops one checkpoint short of the
finish, so the destination is never auto-skipped.

### Validation done so far

- Java change: manually verified against the existing `RoutingController` API and the
  surrounding branch it now falls through to. Not built/tested on device.
- C++ change: control flow extracted into a small dependency-free standalone test
  (attached, `advance_checkpoints_algo_test.cpp`) against a minimal stand-in
  `Checkpoints` class, covering: a single missed checkpoint on a loop route, an
  ambiguous position that must not trigger a skip, confirmation the finish is never
  auto-skipped, multiple consecutive missed checkpoints, and normal tracking where the
  heuristic stays dormant. All 5 pass, compiles clean with `g++ -std=c++23 -Wall
  -Wextra`. Not compiled as part of the actual project (no local toolchain available).
- Member/method names and signatures cross-checked against the real headers via grep,
  not from memory.

**What's still needed:** an actual build + on-device test for both fixes, and review
of the skip-heuristic's threshold/margin choice for Bug 2, since it's a heuristic and
not a precise fix to the position-matching itself.

Patch and standalone test attached.

[organicmaps_fixes.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31119311/organicmaps_fixes.patch)

[advance_checkpoints_algo_test.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31119317/advance_checkpoints_algo_test.cpp)

items.body: The parsing of [additive opening_hours](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:opening_hours/specification#explain:additional_rule_separator), with a `,` and not a `;` like `18:00-23:00, Mo-Sa 11:00-15:00`, seems wrong. Cf screenshot of https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/8929354420 where it should also be opened in the monday-saturday's evenings : ## System * OM version 2022-07-27-3-FDroid * OSM Data 2022-07-18 * LineageOS 18.1 / Android 11

items.title: BUG : incorrect opening_hours display

labels.name: Opening Hours
labels.description: Business Hours, off time, holidays, seasonal

items.body:
**Describe the issue**
Do the opening times show a bug in certain cases?
https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/1046660035

**Steps to reproduce**
1. On a business, set the `opening_hours` tag to `PH,Fr-We 07:00-20:00+` (which is what streetcomplete does)
2. Here's how it looks on organicmaps :
![image](https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/assets/47927025/79b8dc3f-605a-4c15-941b-cd8d19cfa24a)



**Expected behavior**
07:00-20:00 (last client streetcomplete)


**System information:**
 - Operating system and its version: Android 13
 - Organic Maps version: 2023.08.18-8-FDroid (I noticed it the first time on the previous version)
 - Device Model: OnePlus 8 (IN2013)
